summary:
Added a tabbed Settings page for myiotsan (`apps/myiotsan/views/react-webpack/src/views/components/settings.js`) consolidating everything that configures the hub itself -- Users, Location, Notifications, Telemetry, Connectivity, System -- behind one admin-only nav entry, backed by two new runtime-editable settings stores and a system-restart endpoint. `services.NotificationSettingsService` (new `apps/myiotsan/services/notification_settings.go`) persists a delivery config as a JSON blob in the shared RuntimeSetting KV and, critically, is the FIRST code path in the app that ever calls the shared `notification.Service.Configure` -- before this change myiotsan wrote every alert only to its in-app feed regardless of any config, because nothing wired the shared outbound delivery engine up at all. Delivery is now modeled per-DESTINATION rather than a fixed webhook+telegram pair: a new `services.NotificationDestination` (new `apps/myiotsan/services/notification_destination.go`, ported from mymatasan's destination model and scaled down -- the vision-only fields like snapshot mode and template tokens are dropped since a sensor alert has no bounding box or plate) is one delivery target of type webhook, telegram, or mqtt, each with its own minimum-severity floor and a category filter over the two categories myiotsan actually emits (`device.alert`, `system`; empty = all). `NotificationSettings.Destinations` is now authoritative; the original `Webhook`/`Telegram` singleton fields are kept only to migrate an older pre-destinations config forward once (`migrateLegacyDestinations`). New `PUT /api/settings/notification/destination` and `DELETE /api/settings/notification/destination/{id}` (in `apps/myiotsan/apis/settings.go`) upsert or remove one destination without clobbering the others; the existing `GET/PUT /api/settings/notification` and `POST /api/settings/notification/test` are unchanged in shape apart from carrying the new `destinations` array. Saving from the Notifications tab now applies the config to the live hub immediately via `Configure`, and a `Sync` call at boot re-applies a previously-saved config to each fresh process. The Notifications tab itself was rebuilt as an accordion of destinations (one row each, category checkboxes, MQTT broker/topic/QoS/retain/TLS fields where relevant) to match mymatasan's per-destination UI, reusing a newly-ported `AccordionList`/`AccordionItem` (`ui.js`) now shared by both the Notifications tab and AI-adjacent list editors. Alongside this, the whole Settings page was restructured from a single tabbed panel into mymatasan's topic/subtopic layout (a `settings-tab-head` band under the shared Tabs bar, then `settings-panel` subtopic cards), and an earlier UI-consistency regression was fixed suite-wide: an oversized custom `iot-checkbox` class (introduced with the original Settings page) was replaced everywhere with the canonical `check-row` class already used elsewhere in the app, including in `scenes.js` and `schedules.js`'s enabled toggles. `services.TelemetrySettingsService` (new `apps/myiotsan/services/telemetry_settings.go`) persists raw/rollup retention days, write-batcher batch size/flush interval/queue size, and the embedded MQTT broker's listen address (`GET/PUT /api/settings/telemetry`), seeded from `config.json` defaults the first time; `app.go` now reads this store's effective value once at boot (store-over-config) to size `NewReadingWriter`, `telemetry.RunRollup`, and `iotmqtt.New`, replacing direct `config.json` reads at those three call sites -- an edit here does not apply live and needs a restart, which the tab states plainly and links to. A new `apps/myiotsan/apis/system.go` (`NewSystemApi`) adds `POST /api/system/restart` (admin-only, responds 200 before restarting ~500ms later via the shared apphost.Restarter) to make that restart reachable from inside the app. The RBAC catalog (`apps/myiotsan/services/rbac.go`) gained explicit admin-only rows for `/api/settings/notification` (its existing prefix row already covers the new `/destination` sub-routes under the matrix's longest-prefix match), `/api/settings/telemetry`, and `/api/system`, and separately closed a pre-existing gap found alongside this work: `/api/pairing` (fleet key, claim code, adoption status) had never been listed in the catalog at all. The existing site-location panel moved from the Schedules page into the new Settings page (Location tab) with no backend change. Verified live end to end on a booted app: created a user and assigned it a role, set the site location, saved and test-fired a webhook (confirmed delivery was actually configured), saved telemetry retention (confirmed unedited fields kept their defaults), read pairing status, read version/health, then -- for the destinations work -- PUT a webhook destination with categories and a separate MQTT destination, GET reflected both, test-fired (Configure applied), and DELETE removed one destination while leaving the other intact.

Follow-up (frontend-only, no Go/API changes): fixed a CSS gap bug where the Telemetry tab's `<form>` wrapper around its panels lost the `.settings-content` flex column's inter-panel gap (added a matching `.settings-content > form` rule to `styles/iot.css`). Also redesigned the Settings > Users tab from a wall of inline-editable rows into a scannable `DataTable` (initials avatar + name/@username, colour-coded role badge, active/inactive status pill, pending-password-change indicator) with add/edit moved behind a modal dialog and reset-password folded into that same edit modal -- the same admin user-management pattern used elsewhere in the suite. Purely presentational: the same `/api/settings/users` endpoints are called with the same payload shapes.

Follow-up 2 (frontend-only, no Go/API changes): standardized role display across myiotsan so the stored role name `superadmin` always renders as "Administrator" -- matching mymatasan -- instead of the raw internal name; a new `roleLabel(t, name)` helper (`lib/helpers.js`) maps `superadmin`/`operator`/`viewer` to new `role.admin`/`role.operator`/`role.viewer` i18n keys (added to all four locales), falling back to the raw name for any custom role. Used in the side-nav account card and the Users tab's role badge/role picker (`components/layout.js`, `components/settings.js`). Also fixed a CSS gap bug on the Settings > Connectivity tab, where its "Save fleet key" actions row sat flush under the field grid above it with no spacing (`.settings-field-grid + .settings-actions { margin-top: 14px; }` added to `styles/iot.css`). Purely presentational -- no backend, RBAC, or API change; role names and permissions are unchanged, only their on-screen label.
compatibility: Backward-compatible for every existing install: both settings blobs default to safe values (no destinations configured; telemetry defaults taken from the existing config.json values) when no row has ever been saved, so an upgrade changes no runtime behavior until an admin explicitly opts in from the new Settings page. An install that already saved a config under the original single webhook/telegram fields migrates it into the new destination list automatically and transparently the first time it is read (`migrateLegacyDestinations`) -- no action needed and no loss of an existing configured channel. Existing `/api/settings/users`/`/api/settings/roles` behavior is unchanged. The checkbox-class fix and settings-page restructuring are purely visual/markup -- no API or config-shape change. The one-time cost: an admin who wants outbound delivery or changed storage/broker settings must visit the new page and save; telemetry/broker edits additionally require a restart (via the new System tab) to take effect, since those values are still read only at process construction. The Users-tab redesign and Telemetry-tab gap fix are also purely visual/markup with no API, RBAC, or config-shape change -- no admin action needed. The role-label standardization and Connectivity-tab gap fix are likewise purely visual -- no admin action needed, and no stored data changes (only the label shown for the existing `superadmin`/`operator`/`viewer` role names).
